title: An investigation determines that a bomb caused the crash of Air India flight 182.
text: Air India Flight 182 was a scheduled international flight from Toronto Pearson International Airport to Mumbai’s Sahar International Airport with regular Mirabel-London-Delhi stops. On the morning of June 23, 1985, the Boeing 747 serving the Montreal-London segment exploded near the coast of Ireland from a bomb planted by Sikh terrorists from the Babbar Khalsa.

title: The Canadian dollar hits an all-time low of 70.2 U.S. cents on international money markets.
text: The Canadian dollar is the official currency of Canada. There is no standard disambiguating form, but the abbreviations Can$, CA$ and C$ are frequently used for distinction from other currencies, particularly the US dollar.

title: Hinton train collision: 23 people are killed when the Super Continental passenger train collides with a Canadian National Railway freight train near Hinton, Alberta.
text: The Super Continental was a transcontinental Canadian passenger train operated by the Canadian National Railway from 1955 until 1977, when Via Rail took over the train and ran it until it was cancelled in 1981. Service was restored in 1985 but was again eliminated in 1990.

title: Shirley Carr becomes the first female head of the Canadian Union of Public Employees.
text: Shirley Geraldine Edwina Carr was a Canadian union leader who was the first woman president of Canada's largest labour organization, the Canadian Labour Congress.

title: Joe Ghiz becomes premier of Prince Edward Island, replacing James Lee.
text: Joseph Atallah Ghiz was a Canadian politician and lawyer. He was the 27th premier of Prince Edward Island from 1986 to 1993, and was a justice of the Supreme Court of Prince Edward Island from 1995 until his death in 1996.

title: The 1986 World Exposition (Expo 86) in Vancouver opens.
text: The 1986 World Exposition on Transportation and Communication, or simply Expo 86, was a world's fair held in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada from May 2 until October 13, 1986. The fair, the theme of which was "Transportation and Communication: World in Motion – World in Touch", coincided with Vancouver's centennial and was held on the north shore of False Creek.

title: Alberta election: The PCs, led by Don Getty, win a fifth consecutive majority, but a smaller majority than before.
text: Donald Ross Getty was a Canadian athlete, businessman, and politician who served as the 11th premier of Alberta between 1985 and 1992. Before entering politics, Getty had been a quarterback for the Edmonton Eskimos of the Canadian Football League.

title: Roger Coles resigns as leader of Yukon Liberal Party and MLA for Tatchun after being arrested and charged with selling cocaine to an undercover police officer.
text: Roger Coles was a Canadian politician, who represented the electoral district of Tatchun in the Yukon Legislative Assembly from 1985 to 1986. He was a member of the Yukon Liberal Party, and the party's leader from 1984 to 1986.

title: In Vancouver an attempt is made to assassinate Malkiat Singh Sidhu, a cabinet minister in the Indian state of Punjab.
text: Punjab is a state in northwestern India. Forming part of the larger Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent, the state is bordered by the Indian states and union territories of Himachal Pradesh to the north and northeast, Haryana to the south and southeast, Rajasthan to the southwest, Jammu and Kashmir to the north.

title: An accident involving the Mindbender roller coaster at West Edmonton Mall kills three people and seriously injures a fourth.
text: The Mindbender was an Anton Schwarzkopf looping roller coaster at Galaxyland, a theme park in West Edmonton Mall, in Alberta, Canada. The ride officially opened to the public on December 20, 1985 at a cost of $6 million.

title: Jean Drapeau resigns as mayor of Montreal.
text: Jean Drapeau was a Canadian politician who served as mayor of Montreal from 1954 to 1957, and again from 1960 to 1986. Major accomplishments of the Drapeau Administration include the development of the Montreal Metro subway system, the Expo 67 international exposition, and the Place des Arts performing arts centre.

title: Canada adopts sanctions against South Africa for its apartheid policies
text: Apartheidyte, especially South African English: ə-PART-(h)ayt, Afrikaans: ; transl. "separateness", lit. 'aparthood') was a system of institutionalised racial segregation that existed in South Africa from 1948 to 1994. It also existed in South West Africa (now Namibia).

title: Bill Vander Zalm becomes premier of British Columbia, replacing Bill Bennett
text: William Richards Bennett, was a Canadian politician who was the 27th premier of British Columbia from 1975 to 1986.

title: Tamil refugees are found drifting off the coast of Newfoundland
text: The Tamils, also known by their demonym Tamilar, are a Dravidian ethnic group who natively speak the Tamil language and trace their ancestry mainly to the southern part of the Indian subcontinent. Tamil is one of the longest-surviving languages, with over two thousand years of written history, dating back to the Sangam period (between 300 BCE and 300 CE).

title: Elizabeth II augments the coat of arms of Saskatchewan with a crest and supporters
text: Elizabeth II was Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from 6 February 1952 until her death in 2022. She was queen regnant of 32 sovereign states during her lifetime and was the monarch of 15 realms at her death.

title: MPs elect the speaker by secret ballot for the first time.
text: The speaker of the House of Commons is the presiding officer of the lower house of the Parliament of Canada. A member of Parliament (MP), a speaker is elected at the beginning of each new parliament by fellow MPs.
wiki: Speaker of the House of Commons (Canada)

title: Canada receives a United Nations award for sheltering refugees
text: The United Nations is an international intergovernmental organization established by the signing of the Charter of the United Nations on 26 June 1945 with the articulated mission of maintaining international peace and security, to develop friendly relations among states, to promote international cooperation, and to serve as a centre for harmonizing the actions of states in achieving those goals. With 193 member st…

title: Saskatchewan election: Grant Devine's PCs win a second consecutive majority
text: Donald Grant Devine is a Canadian politician who served as the 11th premier of Saskatchewan from 1982 to 1991. He led the Progressive Conservative Party of Saskatchewan from 1979 to 1992.

title: The announcement that the film producer Claude Jutra was reported missing for over one week. He had started to suffer the first symptoms of the Alzheimer's disease.
text: Alzheimer's disease is a neurodegenerative disease and is the most common cause of dementia, accounting for around 60–70% of cases. The most common early symptom is difficulty in remembering recent events.

title: The University of Toronto's John C. Polanyi shares the Nobel Prize for chemistry for the development of the chemical laser.
text: John Charles Polanyi is a German-born Hungarian-Canadian chemist. He was awarded the 1986 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his research in chemical reaction dynamics.

title: Negotiators begin work on what would eventually be the Canada-United States Free Trade Agreement
text: The Canada–United States Free Trade Agreement, official name as the Free Trade Agreement between Canada and the United States of America (French: Accord de libre-échange entre le Canada et les États-Unis d'Amérique), was a bilateral trade agreement reached by negotiators for Canada and the United States on October 4, 1987, and signed by the leaders of both countries on January 2, 1988. The agreement phased out a w…

title: Supreme Court rules on the RWDSU v. Dolphin Delivery Ltd. case
text: The Supreme Court of Canada is the highest court in the judicial system of Canada. It comprises nine justices, whose decisions are the ultimate application of Canadian law, and grants permission to between 40 and 75 litigants each year to appeal decisions rendered by provincial, territorial and federal appellate courts.

title: Conrad Black buys The Daily Telegraph
text: Conrad Moffat Black, Baron Black of Crossharbour is a Canadian and British writer, former politician, newspaper publisher, financier and convicted criminal. Black's father was businessman George Montegu Black II, who had significant holdings in Canadian manufacturing, retail and media businesses through part-ownership of the holding company Ravelston Corporation.

title: Dinosaur fossils are found near Parrsboro, Nova Scotia
text: Dinosaurs are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria. They existed through most of the Mesozoic era, first appearing early in the Triassic period.

title: In an international women's field hockey match at Wembley Stadium (England) Canada beats England 3 – 1.
text: The first Wembley Stadium, originally known as the Empire Stadium, was a football stadium in Wembley, London, England. It opened in 1923 and was demolished in 2002 to make room for the new Wembley Stadium.

title: The Guelph Platers win their only Memorial Cup by defeating the Hull Olympiques 6 to 2.
text: The Memorial Cup is the national championship of the Canadian Hockey League (CHL), a consortium of three major junior ice hockey leagues operating in Canada and parts of the United States. It is a four-team round-robin tournament played among the champions of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL), Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League (QMJHL) and Western Hockey League (WHL), and a host team, which alternates on an annua…

title: The Montreal Canadiens win their 23rd Stanley Cup by defeating the Calgary Flames. The deciding Game 5 is played at Olympic Saddledome in Calgary
text: The Stanley Cup is the championship trophy awarded annually to the National Hockey League (NHL) playoff champion. It is the oldest existing trophy to be awarded to a professional sports franchise in North America, and the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) considers it to be one of the "most important championships available to the sport".

title: Canada participates in the FIFA World Cup for the first time. They would not come back to a World Cup until 2022.
text: The Canada men's national soccer team represents Canada in men's international soccer, and is governed by the Canadian Soccer Association (French: Association canadienne de soccer), the governing body for soccer in Canada founded in 1912. It has been a full member of FIFA since 1912, is a founding member of CONCACAF which was founded in 1961, and is also a member of NAFU in the North American Zone.

title: The UBC Thunderbirds win their second championship by defeating the Western Ontario Mustangs by a score of 25–23.
text: The UBC Thunderbirds are the athletic teams that represent the University of British Columbia. In Canadian intercollegiate competition, the Thunderbirds are the most successful athletic program both regionally in the Canada West Universities Athletic Association, and nationally in U Sports, winning 123 national titles.

title: Hamilton Tiger-Cats win their 7th Grey Cup by defeating the Edmonton Eskimos 39 to 15 in the 74th Grey Cup played at BC Place Stadium in Vancouver
text: The Grey Cup is both the championship game of the Canadian Football League (CFL) and the trophy awarded to the victorious team playing in the namesake championship of professional Canadian football. The game is contested between the winners of the CFL's East and West divisional playoffs and is one of Canadian television's largest annual sporting events.

title: The Canadian Amateur Football Association is renamed Football Canada.
text: Football Canada is the governing body for gridiron football in Canada headquartered in Ottawa, Ontario. Football Canada focuses primarily its own Canadian form of the sport, and is currently the world's only national governing body for Canadian football.

title: Montreal Concordes are re-branded as the "new" Montreal Allouettes
text: The Montreal Alouettes, colloquially known as the Als, are a professional Canadian football team based in Montreal. Founded in 1946, the team has disbanded and been re-established twice.

title: Margaret Atwood - Freeforall
text: Margaret Eleanor Atwood is a Canadian novelist, poet, literary critic, and inventor. Since 1961, she has published 18 books of poetry, 18 novels, 11 books of nonfiction, nine collections of short fiction, eight children's books, two graphic novels, and a number of small press editions of both poetry and fiction.

title: W.P. Kinsella - The Fence Post Chronicles
text: William Patrick Kinsella was a Canadian novelist and short story writer, known for his novel Shoeless Joe (1982), which was adapted into the movie Field of Dreams in 1989. His work often concerned baseball, First Nations people, and Canadian culture.

title: Robert Munsch - Love You Forever
text: Robert Norman Munsch is an American-born Canadian children's author. Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, he moved to Canada in 1975 to work at the University of Guelph.

title: Alice Munro - The Progress of Love
text: Alice Ann Munro was a Canadian short story writer who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2013. Her work tends to move forward and backward in time, with integrated short story cycles.

title: Antonine Maillet - Garrochés en paradis
text: Antonine Maillet was a Canadian novelist, playwright and scholar. She was a member of the Privy Council for Canada and the first non-European recipient of the Prix Goncourt, among other accolades.

title: Hugh Hood - The Motor Boys in Ottawa
text: Hugh John Blagdon Hood, OC was a Canadian novelist, short story writer, essayist and university professor. Hood wrote 32 books: 17 novels including the 12-volume New Age novel sequence (influenced by Marcel Proust and Anthony Powell), several volumes of short fiction, and 5 of nonfiction.

title: William Gibson - Count Zero
text: William Ford Gibson is an American and Canadian speculative fiction writer and essayist widely credited with pioneering the science fiction subgenre known as cyberpunk, a category from which he has repeatedly distanced himself. Beginning his writing career in the late 1970s, his early works were noir, near-future stories that explored the effects of technology, cybernetics, and computer networks on humans, a "comb…

title: See 1986 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: Each winner of the 1986 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit was selected by a panel of judges administered by the Canada Council for the Arts. The four Canada Council Children's Literature Prizes, two each for children's book writers and illustrators, were outside the Governor General's Awards program for the last time.

title: Books in Canada First Novel Award: Wayne Johnston, The Story of Bobby O'Mally
text: Wayne Johnston is a Canadian novelist. His fiction deals primarily with the province of Newfoundland and Labrador, often in a historical setting.

title: Gerald Lampert Award: Joan Fern Shaw, Raspberry Vinegar
text: The Gerald Lampert Memorial Award is an annual literary award presented by the League of Canadian Poets to the best volume of poetry published by a first-time poet. It is presented in honour of poetry promoter Gerald Lampert.

title: Pat Lowther Award: Erín Moure, Domestic Fuel
text: Erín Moure is a Canadian poet and translator with eighteen books of poetry, a co-authored book of poetry, a volume of essays, a book of articles on translation, a poetics, and two memoirs. She has translated or co-translated twenty-one books of poetry and two of biopoetics from French, Spanish, Galician, Portuguese, and Ukrainian, by poets such as Nicole Brossard (with Robert Majzels), Andrés Ajens, Chantal Neveu,…

title: Stephen Leacock Award: Joey Slinger, No Axe too Small to Grind
text: The Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour, also known as the Stephen Leacock Medal for Humour or just the Leacock Medal, is an annual Canadian literary award presented for the best book of humour written in English by a Canadian writer, published or self-published in the previous year. The silver medal, designed by sculptor Emanuel Hahn, is a tribute to well-known Canadian humorist Stephen Leacock and is accom…
wiki: Stephen Leacock Memorial Medal for Humour

title: Vicky Metcalf Award: Dennis Lee
text: Dennis Beynon Lee is a Canadian poet, teacher, editor, and critic born in Toronto, Ontario. He is also a children's writer, well known for his book of children's rhymes, Alligator Pie.

title: Leonard Cohen - First We Take Manhattan
text: Leonard Norman Cohen was a Canadian songwriter, singer, poet, and novelist. Themes commonly explored throughout his work include faith and mortality, isolation and depression, betrayal and redemption, social and political conflict, sexual and romantic love, desire, regret, and loss.

title: Neil Young - Landing on Water
text: Neil Percival Young is a Canadian and American singer-songwriter and musician. Young's deeply personal lyrics and signature high tenor singing voice define his long career.

title: James Cameron's Aliens is released
text: James Francis Cameron is a Canadian and New Zealand filmmaker and explorer. His films combine cutting-edge film technology with classical filmmaking techniques and have grossed over $10 billion worldwide, making him the second highest-grossing film director of all time.

title: David Cronenberg's The Fly
text: David Paul Cronenberg is a Canadian film director, screenwriter, producer and actor. Dubbed "Canada's King of Horror", he is a principal originator of the body horror genre, with his films exploring visceral bodily transformation, infectious diseases, and the intertwining of the psychological, physical, and technological.

title: Denys Arcand's The Decline of the American Empire
text: Georges-Henri Denys Arcand is a Canadian filmmaker. During his four decades career, he became one of the most internationally-recognized directors from Quebec, earning widespread acclaim and numerous accolades for his "intensely personal, challenging, and intellectual films." His film The Barbarian Invasions won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 2004.

title: “Say You, Say Me” by Lionel Richie
text: "Say You, Say Me" is a song written and recorded by American singer and songwriter Lionel Richie for the film White Nights. The single hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and on the Hot Black Singles chart in December 1985.
listen: Say You, Say Me Lionel Richie

title: “Everything in My Heart” by Corey Hart
text: "Everything in My Heart" is a song by Canadian singer Corey Hart. It was released in November 1985 as the third single from Hart's sophomore album, Boy in the Box.
listen: Everything in My Heart Corey Hart

title: “That's What Friends Are For” by Dionne Warwick and Friends
text: "That's What Friends Are For" is a song written by Burt Bacharach and Carole Bayer Sager. It was first recorded by Rod Stewart in 1982 for the soundtrack of the film Night Shift, but it is best known for the 1985 version by Dionne Warwick, Elton John, Gladys Knight, and Stevie Wonder.
listen: That's What Friends Are For Dionne Warwick and Friends

title: “Rock Me Amadeus” by Falco
text: "Rock Me Amadeus" is a novelty song recorded by Austrian musician Falco for his third studio album, Falco 3. The single was made available for physical sale in 1985 in German-speaking Europe, through A&M. "Rock Me Amadeus" was written by Falco along with Dutch music producers Bolland & Bolland.

title: “I Miss You” by Klymaxx
text: "I Miss You" is a song by American R&B and pop group Klymaxx from their fourth album, Meeting in the Ladies Room. Written and co-produced by Klymaxx keyboardist Lynn Malsby, the song was released as the album's third single.

title: “When the Going Gets Tough, the Tough Get Going” by Billy Ocean
text: "When the Going Gets Tough, the Tough Get Going" is a 1985 song co-written and originally recorded by the British singer Billy Ocean in 1985.
wiki: When the Going Gets Tough, the Tough Get Going (song)
listen: When the Going Gets Tough, the Tough Get Going Billy Ocean

title: “Conga” by Miami Sound Machine
text: "Conga" is a song by American band Miami Sound Machine, led by Gloria Estefan, released as the first single from their second English-language album, Primitive Love. The song was written by the band's drummer Enrique Garcia.

title: “How Will I Know” by Whitney Houston
text: "How Will I Know" is a song recorded by American singer Whitney Houston for her self-titled debut studio album. It was released on November 22, 1985, by Arista Records as the album's third single.
listen: How Will I Know Whitney Houston

title: “Kyrie” by Mr. Mister
text: "Kyrie" is a 1985 song by American pop rock band Mr. Mister, from their album Welcome to the Real World.

title: “Sara” by Starship
text: "Sara" is a song recorded by the American rock band Starship which reached number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart on March 15, 1986. It was sung by Mickey Thomas, of the newly renamed band Starship, from their first album Knee Deep in the Hoopla, and Grace Slick provided the backing vocals.

title: “Don't Forget Me (When I'm Gone)” by Glass Tiger
text: "Don't Forget Me" is a song by Canadian rock band Glass Tiger. It was released in 1986 as the lead from their debut album, The Thin Red Line (1986).
listen: Don't Forget Me (When I'm Gone) Glass Tiger

title: “Secret Lovers” by Atlantic Starr
text: "Secret Lovers", released in 1985, is the third single from As the Band Turns, the sixth album from American group Atlantic Starr. "Secret Lovers" was Atlantic Starr's true breakthrough hit on the pop charts in both the US and UK, though the group had previously minor pop and R&B hits in both countries.

title: “Bop” by Dan Seals
text: "Bop" is a song written by Paul Davis and Jennifer Kimball and recorded by American country music artist Dan Seals. It was released in October 1985 as the second single from his fifth studio album, Won't Be Blue Anymore.

title: “The Power of Love” by Jennifer Rush
text: "The Power of Love" is a pop power ballad co-written and first recorded by American singer-songwriter Jennifer Rush in 1984. Released in December 1984 by CBS Records as the fifth single from her debut album, Jennifer Rush, the song became her breakthrough hit and later attracted notable cover versions by Air Supply, Laura Branigan, and Celine Dion.
wiki: The Power of Love (Jennifer Rush song)
listen: The Power of Love Jennifer Rush

title: “Let's Go All the Way” by Sly Fox
text: "Let's Go All the Way" is a song by American new wave duo Sly Fox. Released as a single in 1985 from their debut studio album, Let's Go All the Way, the record became a sleeper hit, entering the top 10 of the singles charts in both the United States and the United Kingdom the following year.
wiki: Let's Go All the Way (Sly Fox song)
listen: Let's Go All the Way Sly Fox

title: “West End Girls” by Pet Shop Boys
text: "West End Girls" is a song by the English synth-pop duo Pet Shop Boys. Written by Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe, the song was released twice as a single.
listen: West End Girls Pet Shop Boys

title: “Live to Tell” by Madonna
text: "Live to Tell" is a song by American singer Madonna from her third studio album, True Blue, and also featured in the crime drama At Close Range, starring her then-husband Sean Penn. Originally composed as an instrumental by Patrick Leonard for the film Fire with Fire, the piece was rejected by Paramount, prompting Madonna to adapt it for At Close Range.

title: “Greatest Love of All” by Whitney Houston
text: "The Greatest Love of All" is a song written by Linda Creed and Michael Masser. Creed wrote the lyrics and Masser composed the music.
listen: Greatest Love of All Whitney Houston

title: “A Different Corner” by George Michael
text: "A Different Corner" is a song written and performed by English singer and songwriter George Michael, released on 24 March 1986 by Epic Records in the UK and Columbia Records in the US. It was Michael's second solo single release following "Careless Whisper", and reached number one on the UK singles chart.

title: “On My Own” by Patti LaBelle and Michael McDonald
text: "On My Own" is a duet by American singers Patti LaBelle and Michael McDonald. It was written and produced by Burt Bacharach and his then-wife Carole Bayer Sager and originally recorded by singer Dionne Warwick for inclusion on her album Friends.
wiki: On My Own (Patti LaBelle and Michael McDonald song)
listen: On My Own Patti LaBelle and Michael McDonald

title: “There'll Be Sad Songs (To Make You Cry)” by Billy Ocean
text: "There'll Be Sad Songs" is a song by Trinidadian-English singer Billy Ocean from his sixth studio album, Love Zone (1986). The song was written and produced by Wayne Brathwaite and Barry Eastmond; Ocean was also credited as a co-writer for the song.
wiki: There'll Be Sad Songs (To Make You Cry)
listen: There'll Be Sad Songs (To Make You Cry) Billy Ocean

title: “I Can't Wait” by Nu Shooz
text: "I Can't Wait" is a song by American group Nu Shooz, included on the band's second album, Tha's Right. The song was remixed by Dutch DJ and producer Peter Slaghuis: this remixed version is the one that appears on the group's 1986 album, Poolside.

title: “Who's Johnny” by El DeBarge
text: "Who's Johnny" is the debut solo single by El DeBarge. Released on April 8, 1986 on the Gordy label, the single was used for the film Short Circuit and reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the Hot R&B Singles chart.

title: “Sledgehammer” by Peter Gabriel
text: "Sledgehammer" is a song by the English rock musician Peter Gabriel. It was released in April 1986 as the lead single from his fifth studio album, So.

title: “Papa Don't Preach” by Madonna
text: "Papa Don't Preach" is a song by American singer Madonna from her third studio album, True Blue. It was written by Brian Elliot and Madonna and produced by Madonna and Stephen Bray.

title: “Glory of Love” by Peter Cetera
text: "Glory of Love" is a song performed by American musician Peter Cetera, which he wrote and composed with his then-wife Diane Nini, and David Foster. The song was recorded by Cetera shortly after he left the band Chicago to pursue a solo career.

title: “Mad About You” by Belinda Carlisle
text: "Mad About You" is a song by American singer Belinda Carlisle. It was written by Paula Jean Brown, James Whelan and Mitchel Young Evans, and produced by Michael Lloyd for Carlisle's debut solo album, Belinda.

title: “Higher Love” by Steve Winwood
text: "Higher Love" is a 1986 song by the English singer Steve Winwood. It was the first single released from his fourth solo studio album, Back in the High Life.

title: “Friends and Lovers” by Gloria Loring and Carl Anderson
text: "Friends and Lovers" is a song written by Jay Gruska and Paul Gordon. The song was first recorded as a duet by Gloria Loring and Carl Anderson in 1985 for the soap opera Days of Our Lives, produced by Doug Lenier.
wiki: Friends and Lovers (Gloria Loring and Carl Anderson song)
listen: Friends and Lovers Gloria Loring and Carl Anderson

title: “Stuck with You” by Huey Lewis and the News
text: "Stuck with You" is a song by American rock band Huey Lewis and the News, written by guitarist Chris Hayes and lead singer Huey Lewis. Released in 1986, it was the first single from the band's fourth album, Fore!
listen: Stuck with You Huey Lewis and the News

title: “Broken Wings” by Mr. Mister
text: "Broken Wings" is a 1985 song recorded by American pop rock band Mr. Mister.

title: “Party All the Time” by Eddie Murphy
text: "Party All the Time" is a song by comedian and actor Eddie Murphy, written and produced by Rick James. It was the lead single from Murphy's 1985 debut musical album How Could It Be.
listen: Party All the Time Eddie Murphy

title: “Burning Heart” by Survivor
text: "Burning Heart" is a song by American rock band Survivor. It appeared in the 1985 film Rocky IV and on its soundtrack album; the film's star Sylvester Stallone personally commissioned the song.

title: “Addicted to Love” by Robert Palmer
text: "Addicted to Love" is a song by the English rock singer Robert Palmer released in 1986. It is the third song on Palmer's eighth studio album Riptide and was released as its third single.

title: “Alive and Kicking” by Simple Minds
text: "Alive and Kicking" is a song by the Scottish rock band Simple Minds, released in September 1985 by Virgin Records as the lead single from their seventh album, Once Upon a Time. The song reached number three on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number four in Canada; it peaked within the top five of several European countries, including Italy, where it reached number one.

title: “Never” by Heart
text: "Never" is a song by American rock band Heart, released on August 29, 1985, as the second single from the band's eponymous eighth studio album. It was written by Holly Knight and Gene Bloch (both from the band Device), and "Connie" (a pseudonym for Ann Wilson, Nancy Wilson, and Sue Ennis).

title: “Kiss” by Prince and The Revolution
text: "Kiss" is a song by American musician Prince. Released by the Paisley Park label as the lead single from Prince and the Revolution's eighth studio album, Parade, on February 5, 1986.

title: “Holding Back the Years” by Simply Red
text: "Holding Back the Years" is a song by the English soul and pop band Simply Red, released as the third single from their debut studio album, Picture Book. In 1986, the ballad reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number two on the UK Singles Chart.
listen: Holding Back the Years Simply Red

title: “Human” by The Human League
text: "Human" is a song by the British synth-pop band the Human League, released as the lead single from their fifth studio album, Crash. The track, which deals with the subject of infidelity, was written and produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis.

title: “Take My Breath Away” by Berlin
text: "Take My Breath Away" is a song written by Giorgio Moroder and Tom Whitlock for the 1986 film Top Gun's soundtrack, performed by American new wave band Berlin and included on their album Count Three & Pray. The song won the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 59th Academy Awards, as well as the Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song at the 44th Golden Globe Awards in 1986.

title: “You Give Love a Bad Name” by Bon Jovi
text: "You Give Love a Bad Name" is a song by American rock band Bon Jovi, released as the first single from their 1986 album Slippery When Wet. Written by Jon Bon Jovi, Richie Sambora, and Desmond Child about a woman who has jilted her lover, the song reached No.
wiki: You Give Love a Bad Name
listen: You Give Love a Bad Name Bon Jovi

title: The World Challenge
text: The World Challenge is a Canadian television documentary series, which aired in English on CBC Television and in French on Télévision de Radio-Canada in 1986. Adapted from Jean-Jacques Servan-Schreiber's 1980 book Le Défi mondial, the six-episode series was hosted by Peter Ustinov and Patrick Watson, and centred on the political and social challenges that threaten the future of humanity.

title: Dear Aunt Agnes
text: Dear Aunt Agnes is a Canadian television comedy-drama series that aired on TV Ontario from January 1986 to December 1989. It was filmed in Toronto, Ontario, and ran for three seasons.

title: Airwaves
text: Airwaves is a Canadian comedy drama television series that aired on CBC Television in 1986 and 1987.

title: The Campbells
text: The Campbells is a period drama television drama series produced by Scottish Television, an affiliate of British television network ITV, and Canadian television network CTV which ran from 1986 to 1990. The series starred Malcolm Stoddard as James Campbell, a Scottish doctor living in 1830s Upper Canada with his three children, seventeen-year-old Neil, fourteen-year old Emma (Amber-Lea Weston) and eleven-year-old J…

title: Adderly
text: Adderly is a Canadian television adventure-drama series which aired from 1986 to 1988. It was broadcast on both Canadian TV and on CBS in the United States.

title: Camp Cariboo
text: Camp Cariboo is a Canadian children's television program that aired on several CTV stations from 1986 to 1989. The show is best known for its rerun stint on YTV from September 2, 1989 to August 15, 1997.

title: Night Walk
text: Night Walk is the first in a short but frequently-repeated series of late-night television programs aired on Global in Ontario from 1986 to 1993. It would later be supplemented by similar programs such as Night Ride and Night Moves.
